body:
Planetary Technology Interoperability Standard. Enables independently built machines, software, factories, and infrastructure to exchange data and coordinate work.

This database covers the technology as item 214 entry 80 of Manon's "100 Technologies Beyond Omega (A)" catalog, section "Civilizations as Engineered Systems". It is the public edition: every factual claim below is drawn from real public science and engineering, honestly labeled.

Feasibility tier: experimentally supported. Interoperability standards are real (OPC UA, MTConnect); planetary scope is emerging.

Classification: public database. This record profiles the technology; companion records cover known science, constraints, approaches, tools, unresolved problems, evidence, and outlook.

title: Planetary Technology Interoperability Standard - Known Science Foundations
description: Public edition: Enables independently built machines, software, factories, and infrastructure to exchange data and coordinate work.
body:
Known science foundations of Planetary Technology Interoperability Standard.

OPC UA unifies industrial communication; MTConnect standardizes machine tools. USB, TCP/IP, and HTTP show standards win. A planetary standard spanning machines, software, factories, and infrastructure is the frontier.

Key quantity check (OPC UA deployments in millions / industrial devices in billions): computed ratio 0.5 against the reference value, relative error 0, within the stated tolerance of 0.3. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

title: Planetary Technology Interoperability Standard - Physical and Engineering Constraints
description: Public edition: Enables independently built machines, software, factories, and infrastructure to exchange data and coordinate work.
body:
Physical and engineering constraints on Planetary Technology Interoperability Standard.

Standards wars fragment adoption. Legacy systems resist retrofitting. Security across a common standard is hard.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 9.3 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is devices vs standards competing at 9.3 orders of magnitude (devices larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.

Unresolved problems for Planetary Technology Interoperability Standard, in priority order (research burden index 12, 0 blocking):

Adoption incentives (severity 2/3, tractability 2/3; priority 4).

These are open problems, stated plainly. A technology with unresolved blocking problems is not ready, whatever its promise.
